ateret-zekenim/1:_: The practice is not to knead matzah for the mitzvah on erev Pesach until after six hours. And it is good to be careful to bake before the festival all the matzot needed for the entire festival; and so is the practice of the meticulous, so that if something chametz becomes mixed in them it will be nullified before Pesach in sixty (Tur).
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: [Levush] After midday etc. — meaning after six and a half, similar to Pesach (Bach); and in Rokeach and Maharil after seven and a half; and it appears to me their reason: we learned the tamid was slaughtered at seven and a half and afterward the Pesach offering; and other poskim hold: since b'dieved it is valid when the Pesach was slaughtered before the tamid, and this mitzvah is only asmakhta, they were lenient l'chatchila; and it appears this is the reason of Magen Avraham who disagrees with Bach and permits after six immediately, since its primary time is after six; and Chok Yaakov challenged from what Magen Avraham wrote beginning siman 433: since we do not know the measure of hours they were stringent until six and a half — see there; and in my humble opinion here is different since it is only asmakhta they were not stringent except unlike minchah prayer. Tur wrote: the meticulous practice to bake everything before Pesach so that if something chametz becomes mixed it will be nullified — end quote; and permitted afterward to cook the matzot on Pesach when mixed in kneading, for if not so even to eat them plain is forbidden (Magen Avraham); and in Matat Moshe he wrote on Tur in the name of R' Shimon it is an excessive stringency; and they also practice to bake on chol ha'moed for honor of Yom Tov that there be fresh matzot, as Maharil wrote; but on the night of Yom Tov itself the view of all Acharonim is not to practice baking for several concerns. Matat Moshe wrote: if one of the matzot was lost he may bake another on Yom Tov even though he has another, lest they were made by minors; and although for afikoman we rely on them as written siman 477, for matzah d'oraisa we do not rely on them — end quote; however if there are still enough there is no concern. Matat Moshe wrote: the baker on the night of Yom Tov should not make doubtful matzot; and all the more so one should not bake from the first night for the second.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [Seif 1] The practice is not to knead etc. — and it is in a responsum: an incident occurred with one who baked matzot before four hours and had already destroyed his chametz, and our rabbis forbade the matzah, for matzah is equated to Pesach; and since Pesach is not slaughtered except from six hours and above, so too matzah. But R' Eliezer the Great and R' Shmuel the priest permitted; however l'chatchila one should be careful for love of the mitzvah in its time. Avi HaEzri brought Tosefta: one fulfills with old matzah provided he made it for Pesach; and he wrote Yerushalmi disagrees with Tosefta and forbids even if he made it for Pesach; and since Yerushalmi forbids, it is fit to be stringent not to make before midday. Tur. And what he wrote that matzah is equated to Pesach as in Pesachim 120b, and Rashi, Rashbam, and Rabbenu Tam wrote there from the verse "on matzot and maror they shall eat it" — see there; and so Levush. And the view of those who permit holds it is not equated to Pesach except for eating but not for making. Bach.
shaarei-teshuvah/1:_: Six hours. Avodat HaKodesh; and R' Yonatan wrote: Acharonim wrote in the name of Rokeach seven and a half; and so in Shibolei HaLeket etc.; and the matter is good to wait until seven and a half; and see Radbaz siman 477 and Eliyah Rabbah and see there who wrote: I saw meticulous people pray minchah before performing the mitzvah, although all year they are concerned for Rambam's view not to pray l'chatchila minchah gedolah on erev Pesach — they would pray before making the matzot — see there; and in our places they do not practice so even among the meticulous, because on erev Pesach when they are completely free after making the matzot there is no concern of forgetting at all; and also no concern they will be delayed in baking more and continue until night, because the bakers of matzot on erev Pesach are zealous; and also per what is explained above siman 432 that now they call to the synagogue — there is no concern lest one be negligent — see there.
yad-ephraim/1:_: (Taz s.k. 1 there) They precede for the mitzvah — end quote; and so ruled Shulchan Aruch etc.; and so practiced Maharshal as above.
